context.note: Marker only. The coordinate is a Wikidata point whose declared precision is about 1 km, so it shows the harbour's neighbourhood, not its quays. Italian Wikipedia places it between the Palatine and Capitoline slopes and says it stayed in use at least to the Flavian period (to AD 96); use at AD 100 is possible, not documented.

Marker only. Pleiades gives this altar no location of its own; its representative point is derived. Foundations possibly lie beneath Santa Maria in Cosmedin (tentative identification). Date range is the Pleiades attestation span, not the altar's origin.

locations.title: Cloaca Maxima · outlet into the Tiber

context.note: Marker only: the mapped mouth of the sewer today, recorded by Pleiades. Pleiades describes a canalised drain from the late sixth century BC draining into the Tiber; the ancient outlet may have lain elsewhere. Lanciani's plate draws the ancient mouth about 15 m east of here, at the river wall (see the Cloaca Maxima drain object).

geometries.title: Ancient ground · illustrative
geometries.note: A neutral tone over the scenario area so no beat shows the modern vegetation plane. It carries no information about ancient terrain, paving or surfaces.

geometries.title: Tiber · modern channel, approximate ancient bank
geometries.note: Modern geometry. OpenStreetMap water outline of today's river, shown only as an approximation of where the ancient bank lay. The present embankments were begun in 1876, so this is not the ancient course.

geometries.title: Forum Boarium · approximate extent
geometries.note: Modern geometry. OpenStreetMap outline of the present-day archaeological site, recorded by Pleiades as its location. Not a surveyed boundary of the ancient market. Date range is the Pleiades record span.

geometries.title: Temple of Hercules Victor · footprint
geometries.note: Modern geometry. Outline of the standing building as mapped in OpenStreetMap (Pleiades location). The temple stands where it did; the outline may omit the base steps. Dated to the later 2nd century BC.

geometries.title: Temple of Portunus · footprint
geometries.note: Modern geometry. Outline of the standing building as mapped in OpenStreetMap (Pleiades location). Pleiades dates the temple to the late 2nd or early 1st century BC.

geometries.title: Pons Aemilius · surviving fragment
geometries.note: Modern geometry. Only the remnant known as the Ponte Rotto is mapped, so this shows where the bridge stood, not its full span. Sources disagree on the first stone bridge: Pleiades says 241 BC, Wikipedia 179 BC begun and 151 BC complete; both precede AD 100.

geometries.title: Arch of Janus
geometries.note: Modern geometry. Early fourth-century arch (Pleiades), so absent at AD 100. Kept in the data so the date filter can show it is left out.

geometries.title: Santa Maria in Cosmedin
geometries.note: Modern geometry. Church founded, by tradition, in the sixth century (Pleiades) and rebuilt from the eighth, so absent at AD 100. Kept in the data so the date filter can show it is left out.
